questions.question: In Parliamentary Procedures: Bills, Majorities & Ordinances, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Ordinary Bill (Art 107/108): Can be introduced in either House. Requires simple majority. Money Bill (Art 110): Introduced ONLY in Lok Sabha with President's prior..."?
questions.explanation: Types of Bills: Ordinary Bill (Art 107/108): Can be introduced in either House. Requires simple majority. Money Bill (Art 110): Introduced ONLY in Lok Sabha with President's prior recommendation. RS has only 14 days to suggest changes (cannot reject). Financial Bill (I) (Art 117(1)): Like Money Bill but can be rejected by RS. Financial Bill (II) (Art 117(3)): Like Ordinary Bill but involves expenditure from Consolidated Fund.

questions.question: In Parliamentary Procedures: Bills, Majorities & Ordinances, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Called by President to resolve deadlock on Ordinary or Financial Bills. NOT available for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills. Presided by Speaker of LS."?
questions.explanation: Joint Sitting (Art 108): Called by President to resolve deadlock on Ordinary or Financial Bills. NOT available for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills. Presided by Speaker of LS.

questions.question: In Parliamentary Procedures: Bills, Majorities & Ordinances, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Simple: >50% of members present and voting. Used for ordinary bills, confidence motion. Absolute : >50% of total membership. Effective : >50% of (Total..."?
questions.explanation: Types of Majorities: Simple: >50% of members present and voting. Used for ordinary bills, confidence motion. Absolute : >50% of total membership. Effective : >50% of (Total membership - Vacancies). Used to remove Speaker/VP. Special : 2/3rd members present and voting + absolute majority. Used for Constitution Amendment (Art 368). Special (Art 61): 2/3rd of total membership. Used for President's Impeachment.

questions.question: In Parliamentary Procedures: Bills, Majorities & Ordinances, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Legislative power of President when both Houses (or one) are not in session. Has same force as an Act. MUST be laid before Parliament when it reassembles. Ceases to..."?
questions.explanation: Ordinance Power (Art 123): Legislative power of President when both Houses (or one) are not in session. Has same force as an Act. MUST be laid before Parliament when it reassembles. Ceases to operate 6 weeks after reassembly. Max life of an ordinance : 6 months + 6 weeks.

questions.question: In Parliamentary Procedures: Bills, Majorities & Ordinances, this exam clue belongs to which area: "A bill pending in LS lapses if LS dissolves. A bill passed by LS but pending in RS lapses. A bill pending in RS but NOT passed by LS does NOT lapse. Bill passed by both..."?
questions.explanation: Lapsing of Bills: A bill pending in LS lapses if LS dissolves. A bill passed by LS but pending in RS lapses. A bill pending in RS but NOT passed by LS does NOT lapse. Bill passed by both Houses pending President's assent does NOT lapse.

lesson_intro: Today we go deeper into the 'Functions' of Parliament. A Parliamentarian's primary job is making laws. But not all bills are the same. A 'Money Bill' (Art 110) has a completely different power dynamic than an 'Ordinary Bill'. We also tackle the 'Types of Majorities'—Simple, Absolute, and Special—which is one of the most confusing yet crucial topics for Prelims. Finally, we look at 'Ordinances' (Art 123), the President's legislative power when Parliament is not in session. Understanding these procedures is the key to understanding how the executive is held accountable by the legislature.
